headline: Nola, bullpen shut out Mets as Phillies win second straight
recap: Aaron Nola threw seven scoreless innings, allowing three hits while striking out four and walking three, and three relievers finished the job as the Phillies blanked the Mets 3-0 in New York. Philadelphia challenged a force play at second base and had the call overturned in the fifth, allowing Bryce Harper's ground single off shortstop Francisco Lindor to stand and drive in Brandon Marsh for a 1-0 lead, with Kyle Schwarber advancing to third and Trea Turner to second. Luis Arraez's sacrifice fly to center fielder A.J. Ewing brought home Turner in the seventh, and Justin Crawford's sacrifice fly to right fielder Carson Benge scored Bryson Stott in the eighth. Jonathan Bowlan, Tim Mayza and Jhoan Duran combined for the final two scoreless innings, with Duran striking out two in a perfect ninth for his 32nd save. Harper went 3-for-4 and Stott had two hits, including a double.
The win was Philadelphia's second straight and moved the Phillies to 85-68 on the season, holding second place in the NL East, four games behind the Atlanta Braves.
The Phillies continue the series against the Mets in New York on Friday, with Andrew Painter starting for Philadelphia opposite Zac Thornton. First pitch is scheduled for 7:15 PM ET at Citi Field.
